title: Warehouse Grain History and Reconciliation
description: Design fact grain and star-schema keys, assign late facts to slowly changing dimensions, and reconcile ETL or ELT measures with worked SQL exercises.

questions.question_text: What is the grain of fact_sale in this lesson?
questions.explanation: A declared fact grain identifies what each row represents.

questions.question_text: Why keep a source sale line identity?
options: To distinguish real events and support idempotent loads
questions.explanation: Event identity preserves legitimate equal measures while detecting repeated loads.

questions.question_text: What does a dimensional surrogate key identify?
options: Every business course forever with no version distinction
A specific dimension record or version
questions.explanation: Dimension keys can distinguish historical versions of one business entity.

questions.question_text: Why can joining a fact to history only by business course ID be wrong?
questions.explanation: History can contain several rows per business identity.

questions.question_text: What is a type 1 dimension change?
options: Always append a new historical version
questions.explanation: Type 1 keeps the chosen current representation rather than preserving each version.

questions.question_text: What is a type 2 dimension change?
options: Retain versions with distinct keys and validity
questions.explanation: Versioned dimensions preserve selected historical attribute changes.

questions.question_text: Which end boundary is used by a half open interval?
questions.explanation: Half open intervals include the start and exclude the end.

questions.question_text: A sale occurs on the new version start date. Which valid adjacent version matches?
questions.explanation: The old exclusive end and new inclusive start avoid a boundary double match.

questions.question_text: Which date should assign a late fact under the stated history contract?
questions.explanation: Historical attribution follows when the business event occurred.

questions.question_text: What is a late arriving dimension issue?
options: The fact arrives before its descriptive dimension is ready
questions.explanation: The fact may need explicit unresolved or unknown-member handling.

questions.question_text: Why not silently discard unresolved facts?
options: Their counts and measures must remain accountable
questions.explanation: Reconciliation needs accepted and rejected or unresolved records to explain the source.

questions.question_text: What does ELT change relative to ETL?
options: Transformation occurs after loading to the destination
questions.explanation: The sequence changes, while correctness obligations remain.

questions.question_text: Why reconcile by course or date as well as total?
options: Only grouped totals are exact integers
Opposite attribution errors can cancel globally
questions.explanation: Local comparisons reveal errors hidden by aggregate cancellation.

questions.question_text: What does load idempotence require?
options: Replay does not create extra logical facts or corrupt corrections
Every run appends all rows again
questions.explanation: Repeat processing must preserve the intended logical outcome.

questions.question_text: Do equal amounts on different sale IDs imply duplicate facts?
questions.explanation: Equality of measures is not event identity.

questions.question_text: Why can SUM(DISTINCT amount) be a bad revenue repair?
options: It removes legitimate equal line amounts
questions.explanation: Distinct amounts are not distinct sales.

questions.question_text: What should be checked before accepting a dimensional join total?
questions.explanation: Zero or multiple matches can omit or multiply measures.

questions.question_text: Does a foreign key alone prove temporal nonoverlap?
questions.explanation: Referential existence does not establish interval validity.

questions.question_text: What is needed before summing mixed-currency amounts?
options: A defined units and conversion policy
questions.explanation: Measures need compatible units to be meaningful.

questions.question_text: What does a reasoned warehouse fixture not prove?
options: An actual executed and reconciled production load
questions.explanation: Runtime and operational evidence require separate execution.

coding_problems.title: Assign Late Sales to Course History
coding_problems.task: Return sale_line_id, department for every staged sale using its sold_on date and the unique matching half-open history interval. Use Unknown when no version matches. History intervals never overlap. Order by sale_line_id.
coding_problems.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE course_history (course_key INT PRIMARY KEY,course_id INT NOT NULL,department VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,valid_from DATE NOT NULL,valid_to DATE NULL); CREATE TABLE staged_sale (sale_line_id INT PRIMARY KEY,course_id INT NOT NULL,sold_on DATE NOT NULL);
coding_problems.solution_sql: SELECT f.sale_line_id,COALESCE(d.department,'Unknown') AS department FROM staged_sale f LEFT JOIN course_history d ON d.course_id=f.course_id AND f.sold_on>=d.valid_from AND (f.sold_on<d.valid_to OR d.valid_to IS NULL) ORDER BY f.sale_line_id;

notes:
## Start with the grain of a fact

A university warehouse reports course sales across years and departments. Before choosing columns, state what one fact row represents. In this lesson one row is one confirmed sale line for one course at one event date. Quantity and amount belong to that line. A report can sum those additive measures across eligible lines. A vague table called statistics with no declared grain invites duplicate loading and totals that mix incompatible levels of detail.

A star schema places a fact relation at the center and descriptive dimensions around it. The course dimension supplies labels and organizational attributes; a date dimension can supply calendar properties. Dimensional keys connect facts to the intended dimension records. The design supports analytical questions, but it does not excuse weak source reconciliation or invented history. A warehouse should make its measures explainable back to defined source events.

## Separate business identity and dimensional identity

A business course identifier identifies the course in its source system. A surrogate dimensional key identifies a particular stored dimension record. Those can differ because one course may have several historical versions. Confusing the two can join a fact to several versions and multiply measures. State which key the fact stores and what historical interpretation that key implies.

The following query assumes the synthetic table definitions and seed data supplied in the practical exercises attached to this topic. Create that exercise fixture first; the query fragment is not a standalone database setup.

```sql
CREATE TABLE dim_course (
 course_key INT PRIMARY KEY,
 course_id INT NOT NULL,
 course_title VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
 department VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE fact_sale (
 sale_line_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
 course_key INT NOT NULL,
 sold_on DATE NOT NULL,
 quantity INT NOT NULL,
 amount INT NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO dim_course VALUES
 (101,10,'Databases','Computing'),(201,20,'Design','Arts');
INSERT INTO fact_sale VALUES
 (1,101,'2026-01-10',1,100),
 (2,101,'2026-01-10',1,100),
 (3,201,'2026-01-11',2,160);
```

The first two lines have equal values but distinct sale identities. They are both valid contributions unless the source contract says otherwise. Removing duplicate amount and date combinations would reduce Computing revenue from 200 to 100 incorrectly. A unique source event or line key supports idempotent loading without collapsing legitimate equal measures.

## Additive measures need a clear contract

SUM(amount) gives 200 for Computing and 160 for Arts in the sample. SUM(quantity) gives two units in each department. Averaging line averages is not generally a meaningful weighted result. A unit price measure should be derived using the appropriate amount and quantity totals when that matches the business definition. Ratios, balances, and distinct customer counts have different aggregation behavior from ordinary additive amounts.

```sql
SELECT d.department,SUM(f.amount) AS revenue
FROM fact_sale f JOIN dim_course d ON d.course_key=f.course_key
GROUP BY d.department ORDER BY d.department;
```

These expected outputs are derived from the fixture rather than an executed warehouse job. Define currency, refund treatment, taxes, event eligibility, and date interpretation before extending this arithmetic to real revenue. Combining amounts in different currencies without a conversion policy produces a number but not a meaningful reconciled measure. A warehouse query must preserve units as well as row identities.

## Slowly changing dimensions preserve chosen history

A type 1 dimension change overwrites a descriptive attribute, so reports generally display the latest stored label. A type 2 approach retains versions with separate surrogate keys and effective intervals. The choice follows reporting requirements: does a sale belong under the department as known when it occurred, or under today's organization? Both questions can be legitimate, but they require clearly distinguished contracts.

A type 2 course history might move course 10 from Computing to Data Science on February 1. The old version covers dates before February 1 and the new version begins on that date. Use half open intervals: valid_from is inclusive and valid_to is exclusive. That makes an event on the boundary belong to one version when intervals are valid. Adjacent versions can meet without overlapping.

```sql
SELECT f.sale_line_id,d.course_key,d.department
FROM staged_sale f
LEFT JOIN course_history d
 ON d.course_id=f.course_id
 AND f.sold_on >= d.valid_from
 AND (f.sold_on < d.valid_to OR d.valid_to IS NULL)
ORDER BY f.sale_line_id;
```

NULL valid_to means an open ended version under this explicit convention. It is not automatically earlier or later than every date in ordinary comparisons. The OR handles that chosen meaning. The history must also prevent overlapping versions for the same course; otherwise one fact can match multiple rows. A foreign key to a dimension key alone does not enforce every temporal interval rule.

## Late arriving facts and dimensions

A late arriving fact is received after the period in which its event occurred. Historical attribution should normally use the event date under the stated reporting contract, not the load date. A sale received in March but occurring in January can belong to the old department version. Loading it against only the current dimension can silently rewrite historical meaning.

A late arriving dimension means a fact arrives before its descriptive record is ready. Strategies include quarantining the fact for resolution or assigning an explicitly defined unknown member and repairing attribution later. Do not invent a plausible course label or silently discard the amount. Track unresolved identities and the effect of later corrections. Whether reports are restated must be a deliberate policy.

Optional descriptive labels and missing keys are also different. A valid dimension record can have an unavailable optional description. An unmatched mandatory course reference indicates a relationship issue. Use separate diagnostics so COALESCE to Unknown does not conceal a growing load defect. A friendly display label is not a successful reconciliation.

## ETL and ELT still need validation

ETL transforms before loading the analytical destination; ELT loads first and transforms there. Neither sequence guarantees correctness. Both need source boundaries, type validation, identity rules, duplicate handling, rejected-row accounting, and repeatable transformations. Record which batch and source interval produced a fact, so operators can explain both included and excluded rows.

A useful reconciliation checks counts and sums at the declared grain. If the source contains three eligible lines totaling 360, the accepted warehouse facts plus documented rejects should explain all three and the total. Compare grouping by course or date as well as the grand total: two opposite attribution errors can cancel globally. Check key uniqueness and dimension match counts before accepting measure sums.

Idempotence means replaying the same logical load does not create additional facts or corrupt newer corrections. A unique source line identity can support upsert or controlled replacement, depending on policy. A timeout alone does not prove a load failed. Retry behavior and batch checkpoints must be designed so uncertain completion is safe to investigate and repeat.

## Keep an audit boundary for corrections

A corrected source amount requires a defined update policy. Some warehouses replace a fact with the latest authoritative value; others record explicit adjustment events. Either can be valid when reports, reconciliation, and historical restatement rules agree. Keep source identity and correction provenance so an operator can explain why a previously published period changed. Replaying an old batch must not silently undo a newer approved correction.

## Worked lab: reconcile department revenue

The first task groups the sample facts by their course dimension department. Join on the surrogate course_key, sum every amount, and order by department. The solution returns Arts 160 and Computing 200. Test two equal sale amounts, a department with no fact rows, and multiple courses sharing one department. Decide separately whether a report should show departments with zero revenue; an inner join does not create them.

To investigate a mismatch, count matches per sale line before grouping. More than one dimension match can multiply revenue even if each fact was loaded once. An unmatched dimension can remove revenue under an inner join. These diagnostics localize the problem instead of repairing the final sum with DISTINCT, which can discard valid equal amounts.

## Worked lab: assign a late fact to history

Course 10 has version 101 before February 1 and version 102 from February 1 onward. A sale dated January 31 maps to 101; a sale dated February 1 maps to 102, even if both are loaded in March. The solution uses event date and the half open interval predicates shown above. Include an unmatched course and keep it visible with a left join for investigation.

Reject overlapping history as a separate integrity defect rather than choosing an arbitrary version. Verify exactly one eligible match for resolved facts, preserve unresolved identifiers, and reconcile totals after assignment. Continue with [Transitive Dependency](/learning/dbms-sql-tutorial/transitive-dependency) for fact ownership and [View Maintenance](/learning/dbms-sql-tutorial/view-maintenance) for stored-result reconciliation. This foundation prepares warehouse reasoning without claiming a completed pipeline or executed load.
